lines.text: We buried Dunn on a grey morning, beside the Measurer we had buried in the summer. His stone was bigger. Bram made sure of it.
He talked too much. He joked at the worst possible times. He never once listened to me.
He was the bravest idiot I ever knew. And I would give anything to hear him say something stupid right now.
Half the village laughed. The other half cried. Most of us did both. Dunn would have liked that.
On top of his stone lay a soldier's badge, in the King's colours. The boy from the wall had left it there, before the column rode south.
I told you I'd bring them all back, Bram.
Nobody brings them all back, my lord. Not forever. You went, and you tried, and every one of them knew it.
That afternoon, I laid the Compact on the table again. I didn't make a speech. I didn't have one left.
Kesting signs. First. And any man who laughs at it can answer to me.
Marrick signs. Ten parts in a hundred of Saltmouth, one bathhouse, and your farmers at my harvest. I wrote it in the margin, Lord Lucan, in case you forget.
Freydis, the Skeld elder, looked Halvard's bearskin up and down. He looked at hers. Neither of them said a word. It was the most respectful thing I have ever seen.
The Skeld do not write. We remember. Let the paper remember too.
I signed last. My fingers were still black. It was the worst signature of my life.
And the lamp above us jumped. Brighter than it had ever been.
Still five at the ceiling. But the whole north just tied itself to you. Everything under it will grow faster now. Everything.
Kesting. Marrick. Greyhollow. The Skeld. The first Compact the north had made in three hundred years.
Now you're dangerous, my lord.
Is that good?
That depends on who's afraid.
Far to the south, someone was very afraid.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fifty-eight, coming soon.
